title: The Biggest Wooden Plane Ever Built Flew Exactly Once, Under a Minute

scenes.text: The biggest wooden plane ever flew exactly once.
The Spruce Goose had a 320-foot wingspan, longer than a football field. It was wood because of wartime steel limits.
On November 2, 1947, Howard Hughes flew it over Long Beach Harbor.
It stayed in the air for less than a minute, a few dozen feet above the water.
Then it landed, and it never flew again.
And the name? Critics came up with Spruce Goose. It was mostly birch.

description:
The Spruce Goose, the biggest wooden plane ever built, flew exactly once.
Howard Hughes flew it on November 2, 1947, over Long Beach Harbor for less than a minute. It has a 320-foot wingspan and is made mainly of birch, not spruce.
Would you have flown in it? Comment below.
first_comment: Accounts disagree on exactly how far and high it flew, but not on one thing: it never flew again. Would you have flown it?
